title: Some async code doesn't produce stack trace on error

> It seems this is a JavaScriptCode bug, if the function is async, JSC cannot produce the full stack trace.

NodeJS has the same issue of not resolving stack traces across async calls. It makes debugging a lot harder than it needs to be. But in NodeJS you can use the `bluebird` library to replace the Promise implementation with one that does allow for stack traces to include promises. Unfortunately bluebird doesn't work in bun.

#11948 seems to do something similar to what bluebird does. What is the reasoning for not merging it? Would it be possible to implement this as a library for bun, similar to what bluebird does for NodeJS?

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
We’ve actually spent a bunch of time thinking about how to fix this 

it’s a JSC thing

there are a few different approaches. we can’t exactly copy what v8 did for zero cost async stacktraces because JSC’s implementation of async functions is different (there’s no lingering reference to the AsyncFunction object, just the generator which has no way to get what the function name calling it was)

we could make this work for just the immediate top level task that started the current run. For example, awaiting a Bun.file(path).text() call. It would be missing any promises between that call and the previous microtask run (the previous await). This would be pretty cheap to track because it would only work for natively implemented functions, not user code. So you’d know that the error came from code that read a file, you would know where it threw before that promise maybe, but not much else in between 

We could also make it only work in —inspect. we already wired up async stack traces to the inspector. It’s too expensive to do at runtime normally, but if you use the web inspector it should track everything

It is enough for them to see this thread to conclude that this deal breaking feature is not going to get fixed in predictable future. I deleted my previous rant about this and switched to node a month before release because I cannot afford lack of error stack in commercial platform. comments.author: participant19
comments.body:
Ok, I have an idea.

Based on my understanding, Bun has a fork of JavascriptCore where they are adding cool new features.

But I think for version 2, we need to have our own Javascript interpreter. There are three key things it would need:

- static type optimization (for typescript - free performance)
- goroutines (would require a bit more syntax but necessary for any modern backend)
- python compatibility

I have started an experimental repo to create a JIT for typescript that is faster than V8 due to the ability to use raw TS types. I think also we need it to support slice syntax so that JS can stay relevant in the age of AI.

Please take a look at this repo and let me know if you think that it would be something you all would be interested in applying to Bun.

https://github.com/participant19/ultrascript

I haven't started python compatibility, but I think it should be able to import python files and pip modules for max compatibility.

I wrote it in a couple weeks using Claude Code, so it's pretty easy to keep going and update.

comments.author: participant18
comments.body:
The fix in 1.2.22 is nice and very helpful, but still slightly incomplete: it doesn't show callsites in module root. Repro:

```js
async function one() {await two()}

async function two() {await three()}

async function three() {
  await four()
  throw Error(`some_error`)
}

async function four() {}

await one()
```

Output in Bun 1.2.22; module root line is missing:

```
2 |
3 | async function two() {await three()}
4 |
5 | async function three() {
6 |   await four()
7 |   throw Error(`some_error`)
            ^
error: some_error
      at three (<path>:7:9)
      at async two (<path>:3:29)
      at async one (<path>:1:29)
```

Output in Deno; module root line is present:

```
error: Uncaught (in promise) Error: some_error
  throw Error(`some_error`)
        ^
    at three (file://<path>:7:9)
    at async two (file://<path>:3:23)
    at async one (file://<path>:1:23)
    at async file://<path>:12:1
```

This has a small effect on testing. Admittedly the severity is minor.
